title: Lamb Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs baked in spiced lamb and tomato sauce
excerpt: Spiced lamb mince in a rich, deeply flavoured tomato and pepper sauce with eggs poached directly in it. Finished with crumbled feta and fresh parsley, this is a bold, filling one-pan dish for any time of day.
sourceNotes: Shakshuka, meaning 'all mixed up' in Arabic, is a staple of North African and Middle Eastern cooking that has become a globally popular brunch and supper dish. The addition of lamb mince to the classic tomato sauce is common in Turkish and Libyan versions of the dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb and tomato base can be made up to 2 days ahead. Reheat, add eggs, and finish as below.

content.text: Use the largest frying pan you have so there is room for all six eggs without them merging. Make wells in the sauce before cracking the eggs in; this keeps the yolks centred and the whites contained. Cover the pan with a lid for the last stage so the egg whites set while the yolks stay runny.
Heat the olive oil in the large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the lamb mince and cook, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes until well browned. Drain off any excess fat.
Add the onion and peppers. Cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and spices and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and crush them roughly. Season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Make six wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook over a low-medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are just set but the yolks are still runny. Check frequently.
Remove from the heat and scatter over the crumbled feta and fresh parsley. Serve directly from the pan with flatbread or crusty bread.

items.cause: The pan was too hot or the lid was on too long.
items.fix: Cook on low heat and check every 2 minutes; remove lid early.

items.symptom: Egg whites are still clear and runny around the yolk.
items.cause: The sauce was not hot enough when the eggs went in.
items.fix: Bring sauce to a simmer before adding eggs; keep heat steady.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and the eggs are sinking.
items.cause: The tomato sauce reduced too much before eggs were added.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to loosen the sauce before adding eggs.
